about.intro: I'm a PhD researcher at the Institute of Communication and Computer Systems (ICCS), National Technical University of Athens, working on efficient AI inference for resource-constrained and distributed environments.
rows: Doctoral Researcher, ICCS, National Technical University of Athens
f-inference — Efficient Foundation Model Inference Across the Computing Continuum
Efficient inference for large language and foundation models
Researcher, Ericsson Research AI · MS by Research, IIIT Hyderabad
bio: My research sits where systems meet machine learning: how large language models can be made leaner in what they store, move and compute, without losing the reasoning quality that makes them useful.

Before Athens I completed an MS by Research at IIIT Hyderabad, building TRAQID, a 26,678-image traffic air-quality dataset, and AQIFormer, a transformer that classifies AQI across cities. At Ericsson Research AI I worked on network-aware path planning for factory robots in the Horizon Europe PANDORA project.

I believe inference efficiency is the bottleneck between lab-scale models and real deployment, and the most interesting work lives at that boundary. Outside research: cricket, hockey, badminton, hiking, and writing short stories and poetry.

project.name: f-inference
project.full: Efficient Foundation Model Inference Across the Computing Continuum
paras: Foundation models are trained on broad data and adapt to tasks across text, images, audio, video and time series — but running them today depends on centralised cloud providers, costs a lot of energy and money, and adds latency.

f-inference builds a Resource-driven Computing Continuum that distributes foundation-model inference across Cloud, Edge and IoT, moving it closer to data and users through adaptive, efficient inference — cutting latency, energy and cost while preserving data sovereignty, and opening advanced GenAI to SMEs and resource-constrained communities.
challenges: Dependence on centralised cloud providers, threatening digital sovereignty and data security
High energy demands that conflict with sustainability goals
Costs that exclude SMEs from deploying and customising models
Remote services that add latency and single points of failure

research.title: Efficient inference for large language models
research.desc: Large language models are powerful but costly to run: their sheer size, attention that grows quadratically with input length, and token-by-token decoding drive up latency, memory and energy. My research makes LLM inference leaner across the data, model and system levels — reducing what a model stores, moves and computes — so it runs fast and reliably on constrained hardware, closer to where the data lives.

research.title: Network-aware path planning for industrial robots
research.desc: Factory robots are limited by wireless quality as much as by floor space. With Ericsson Research AI I built a Sionna ray-tracing framework validated on real measurements (R² = 0.87) and planners that co-optimise path cost and coverage; a spatial-aware transformer predicts SNR within 2.31 dB and runs 31× faster than GNN baselines.

research.title: Visual air-quality intelligence
research.desc: Estimating air quality from street-level images removes the dependency on expensive sensor networks. I built TRAQID — 26,678 front and rear traffic images with co-located AQI and weather data — and AQIFormer, a multi-view transformer reaching 89.96% accuracy and 81.67% on a city unseen in training.

research.title: Remote, vision-evaluated laboratories
research.desc: A platform that lets students run real physics experiments over the internet, with computer vision measuring the outcome — about 10× lower error than infrared sensing. It served thousands of learners and led to a FiCloud 2022 paper and a US patent.
